messages:
chris_cust: Hey team — got charged via AWS Marketplace for ~3x our expected token usage in March. Invoice line items show a 'Redwood Inference - tokens' SKU with a huge quantity. Can someone explain?
anya_support: Sorry about that — can you attach the invoice PDF or paste the line item rows? also which account/org id did you use to sign up?
chris_cust: Attached the invoice snippet: 

product_code: AWSPROD-12345
usage_type: tokens
quantity: 2,984,512
unit_price: 0.0001
line_total: $298.45

We signed up with org id rwd-42; marketplace account is linked to our AWS payer account 987654321000.
anya_support: thx. looping billing: @mike_billing can you reconcile our metering events vs marketplace export? common issue is meter_id mapping to the wrong customer.
mike_billing: Looking at our marketplace export for March, I see two meter_ids tied to the same product_code: m-abc123 and m-xyz789. m-xyz789 has usage from an internal test org (rwd-int-test) that should not map to customer rwd-42. Suspect attribution mismatch during onboarding.
anya_support: does that explain 3x multiplier?
mike_billing: yes — internal test usage (~1.9M tokens) was billed under the customer's marketplace subscription because the meter_id for the private deploy used the customer's subscription token when we created the instance. I can show query: 

```
SELECT metering_event_id, meter_id, account_id, tokens_reported
FROM marketplace_usage
WHERE invoice_period = '2026-03'
  AND product_code = 'AWSPROD-12345'
  AND account_id IN ('rwd-42','rwd-int-test');
```

This returns two clusters. The test cluster was routed to the customer's AWS subscription.
devon_sre: I checked runtime logs — there is a race in onboarding where the marketplace entitlement lookup falls back to a default org for non-idempotent deploys. I filed a bug PR to add a stricter entitlement cache and to validate `subscription_id` at instance start. Patch in review.
lina_eng: Opened a quick query to map marketplace consumption to our internal invoices: `aws_marketplace_export.csv` has a column `usage_dimensions` and `metering_id`. I matched metering_id -> internal org and confirmed the misattributed rows.
achron: (bot) invoice-attach: invoice_2026-03-01.pdf (uploaded)
anya_support: Next steps: 1) file AWS support case to request reversal/credit for the misattributed m-xyz789 usage; 2) issue provisional credit to customer while AWS processes; 3) fix onboarding entitlement mapping to prevent recurrence.
chris_cust: Appreciate that — timeline? We can't absorb this unexpected $298.45.
mike_billing: Filing AWS case now, will include export csv and our reconciliation table. Case ref: 123456789012345. I'll also ask for expedited review since it's attribution error.
anya_support: I'll approve a provisional customer credit for $300 pending AWS confirmation. Will post internal invoice adjustment once AWS confirms reversal.
aws-billing-bot: AWS Support case 123456789012345 created. Initial response ETA 48 hours.
devon_sre: Patch merged to staging; rollout to production scheduled in next deploy window (in ~2 hours). This will stop future misattribution but won't affect past events.
anya_support: mike — after AWS replies, please share their CSV reconciliation so we can reconcile ledger entries and finalize the credit. chris_cust: we'll update you as soon as we have AWS confirmation; provisional credit applied now. Sorry for the noise and thanks for flagging. :pray:
chris_cust: Thank you all — provisional credit shows up on our dashboard. Please keep me posted.
anya_support: will do. closing loop when AWS resolves.
